answer: A new identity must climb a trellis of interdependent verification tasks: each task is assigned by a different random verifier, and the kernel output of one task becomes the input of the next, so tasks cannot be skipped or run in parallel by one operator. Standing on a knoll, a single honest agent sees one clear path and climbs it in ordinary work time. A sybil farmer faces a thousand separate trellises, each demanding sequential real work and distinct verifier approvals, so the total labor scales linearly with fake count while honest cost stays flat.
